free_tier.stated: 200 GB per dataset (hard, public or private), 50 top-level files per dataset, 200 GB max total PRIVATE datasets. There is NO documented aggregate cap on public datasets. The docs' 'Technical Specifications' section states only '200GB per dataset limit', '200GB max private datasets', 'A max of 50 top-level files'. Public total is therefore effectively unlimited per account, and the 200 GB/dataset ceiling is raised on request (see quota-program candidate).

egress.terms: Free and CDN-backed: the download endpoint 302s to a signed storage.googleapis.com URL (Google Cloud Storage), which is Fastly/Google-fronted. No egress quota documented, no per-GB charge, no auth needed for public datasets.

record.tooling: Kagglehub (pip install kagglehub, official, github.com/Kaggle/kagglehub). Resolves public datasets with NO credentials; kaggle-api CLI (`kaggle datasets download -d owner/slug`); plain HTTPS + curl/wget against /api/v1/datasets/download/<owner>/<slug>; rclone can front the signed GCS URL with an HTTP remote.
record.chaining: 200 GB x unlimited public datasets x unlimited free accounts. Live proof of the unlimited-public side: one account holds 23 public datasets totalling 1,197.7 GB with a largest single dataset of 163.0 GB (API-verified). I.e. 6x over the 200 GB 'private quota' figure, so the private quota demonstrably does not apply to public datasets. Multiply again by Kaggle Organizations (a dataset can be owned by an org the account belongs to) and by the free quota-request program for >200 GB single datasets.
record.limits_note: 200 GB/dataset; 50 top-level files per dataset (use a directory tree or a ZIP. Kaggle unzips archives server-side and the unzipped size counts); each new version adds a full copy so versioned datasets consume quota per version and old versions cannot be deleted (documented user complaint, unresolved); dynamic rate limiting on the API (HTTP 429). Dataset ingestion of a >100 GB upload via the web UI/API is flaky. Kaggle staff recommend creating from a remote URL or GCS bucket instead.
record.reliability_note: Stable, corporate-owned (Google), no history of quota clawback; the failure modes are ingestion flakiness on very large uploads and un-deletable old versions, not data loss.

record.notes: The amount is unverified by design: 'a very high complimentary compute quota' carries no number on any page read, so the record claims the mechanism and not the size. Three explanations for why the quota exists were considered: it subsidises benchmark supply for Kaggle's leaderboards, it is developer marketing for the model providers, and it replaces engineering work the labs would otherwise do. record.provider: Kaggle Notebook outputs (/kaggle/working) — the free side-channel

free_tier.stated: Up to 20 GB of output per notebook version saved to /kaggle/working, and every 'Save & Run All' creates a new version. Outputs are themselves addable as dataset inputs to any future notebook. No documented cap on the number of notebook versions or notebooks per account.

retention.stated: | Outputs persist indefinitely and are downloadable years later; the flaky part is the commit step (a timed-out run loses the output).

egress.terms: Free download of notebook output files from the version's Output tab, same GCS-backed delivery.

record.tooling: kaggle CLI (`kaggle kernels output <owner>/<kernel> -p ./dir`) and kagglehub. The notebook executes on managed GPU and TPU compute, writing files directly on the host without local upload transfer.
record.chaining: 20 GB per notebook version. Notebook versions, notebooks and accounts each carry no stated limit. The reachable total therefore scales with versions and notebooks per account, and a second account carries a second allowance. The whole write path is server-side (the data is produced or fetched inside the notebook, so there is no client uplink bottleneck). This is the standard community alternative route around the 200 GB private quota: a Kaggle forum answer describes it as 'create a new notebook from your dataset and copy files to /kaggle/working'.
record.limits_note: 20 GB per version is hard; 9 h / 12 h session limits per run; output is only persisted on commit ('Save & Run All'), not on interactive save; GPU/TPU hours are rationed (~30 h/week) but CPU-only runs are not the constraint for pure storage.
record.reliability_note: Outputs persist indefinitely and are downloadable years later; the flaky part is the commit step (a timed-out run loses the output).
